summary.en: Israel’s forces have recently destroyed an underground Hezbollah infrastructure in south Lebanon and a Hezbollah tunnel in Shebaa, while also launching operations in central Gaza and a Hamas-controlled area of Gaza. Iraq has moved its army into a stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah, linking the regional fight to the Israel-Hezbollah clash. Hezbollah and Iran have recruited Thai clerics for a foiled plot to attack the Israeli embassy in Bangkok, and Israeli officials have threatened to seize more territory in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria. The World Bank notes Lebanon’s reconstruction is proceeding slowly, and the UCDP recorded 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024.
summary.nb: Israels styrker har nylig ødelagt en underjordisk Hizbollah-infrastruktur i Sør-Libanon og en Hizbollah-tunnel i Shebaa, samtidig som de har igangsatt operasjoner i sentrale Gaza og et Hamas-kontrollert område i Gaza. Irak har flyttet hæren inn i et festningsverk til den Iran-støttede Kataib-Hezbollah, og knytter den regionale kampen til konflikten mellom Israel og Hizbollah. Hizbollah og Iran har rekruttert thailandske prester til et avlyst plot mot den israelske ambassaden i Bangkok, og israelske tjenestemenn har truet med å erobre mer territorium i Gaza, Libanon og Syria. Verdensbanken bemerker at Libanons gjenoppbygging går sakte, og UCDP registrerte 4 335 dødsfall i kamper i 2024.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
